title: Forge 9: Conv2D and max-pool with hand-written backward

wrong.flipped_kernel.py: the kernel is flipped (true convolution); forward and gradients stay self-consistent but values differ from the cross-correlation every framework implements
wrong.overwrite_overlaps.py: dx is assigned instead of accumulated, so overlapping windows overwrite each other
wrong.dx_keeps_padding.py: dx is returned with the zero padding still attached, so its shape is wrong
wrong.db_first_example.py: db uses only the first example instead of summing over the batch
wrong.dw_mean_over_batch.py: dW is averaged over the batch; that scaling belongs to the loss
wrong.accumulating_grads.py: dW accumulates across backward calls instead of being set
wrong.backward_stride_one.py: backward scatters as if stride were 1
wrong.init_unscaled.py: W ~ Normal(0, 1) instead of Normal(0, 1/(in_ch*k*k)): activations grow with the receptive field
wrong.pad_one_side.py: padding is added only on the top and left
wrong.pool_grad_to_whole_window.py: every input in a window receives the output's gradient, not just the winner
wrong.pool_average_gradient.py: the gradient is split evenly (average-pool backward) although the forward takes the max
wrong.pool_ties_split.py: every input tied for the maximum receives the full gradient, so gradient mass is not conserved
wrong.pool_ignores_stride.py: the stride argument is ignored: windows never overlap
wrong.pool_overlap_overwrite.py: with overlapping windows an input that wins two windows keeps only one of the two gradients

hints: Do not loop over output pixels. Build an im2col matrix: for each of the k*k kernel offsets (i, j), slice the padded image with a stride, `xp[:, :, i:i+s*Ho:s, j:j+s*Wo:s]`. Stack them to (N, C*k*k, Ho*Wo) and the whole layer becomes one matmul with W reshaped to (out_ch, C*k*k).
Output size is (H + 2*pad - k) // stride + 1. np.pad with ((0,0),(0,0),(pad,pad),(pad,pad)) pads only the two spatial axes.

Backward mirrors forward: dW is the same matmul as Linear's x.T @ dout, only on columns; db sums dout over batch and both spatial axes; dcols = W.T @ dout. Then un-fold dcols with the same strided slices, adding (+=) because neighbouring windows read the same pixel. Finally crop the padding.

Max-pool backward: remember argmax over the window offsets in forward. In backward, each output sends its gradient to the offset that won, and nothing to the others. Overlapping windows (stride < size) add up again.
Check one thing at a time with finite differences: dx with stride 2 and padding 1 catches most scatter bugs; compare the sum of dx with the sum of the upstream for pooling.
